claims.text: As-cast WTaTiVZr has a naturally segregated, dual-phase dendritic microstructure.
The dendrites are W-Ta-rich, the interdendritic regions are Zr-Ti-rich, and V is distributed between both regions.
The segregated dual-phase dendritic microstructure is the primary cause of WTaTiVZr's enhanced plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten.
Multicomponent solid-solution strengthening and lattice distortion in the W-Ta-rich dendrites provide high strength.
The Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions facilitate localized plastic deformation.
The Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions modify dislocation-core behavior.
The Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions increase grain-boundary cohesion.
Localized deformation in the interdendritic regions impedes crack propagation and increases damage tolerance.
The dual-phase interaction lowers the brittle-to-ductile transition temperature relative to single-phase pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will have higher yield strength than powder-sintered pure tungsten at room temperature and elevated temperatures up to 500 °C.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten, especially above 200 °C.
WTaTiVZr will show less scratch-induced cracking and higher scratch-derived fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
The commercial powder-sintered pure-tungsten baseline has a single-phase BCC microstructure with coarse equiaxed grains of approximately 100 ± 20 µm.
The pure-tungsten baseline has an indentation-derived yield strength of approximately 700 MPa at room temperature and 250 MPa at 500 °C.
The pure-tungsten baseline has negligible plasticity below 300 °C.
The pure-tungsten baseline has a scratch-based fracture toughness of approximately 25 ± 1 MPa√m.

The proposed advantage applies under quasi-static compression, indentation from room temperature to 500 °C, and the specified scratch-testing conditions, but is not claimed below room temperature or under irradiation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes the property difference primarily to dendritic segregation, but the proposed comparison changes composition, processing route, phase constitution, and grain morphology simultaneously by comparing arc-melted WTaTiVZr with powder-sintered pure tungsten. It therefore does not isolate segregation from chemistry or processing as the causal variable.
